rows: If you are a white-tailed deer, you have one cone most sensitive at 450 to 460 nanometers and one at 537. A human has three kinds, and you have two. Blues and yellow-greens stay apart for you, and orange and red can still be told from them.

If you are a white-tailed deer, the finest detail you resolve lies between 4 and 6 cycles per degree. A human reads about 30 on an eye chart. Fences, faces and the edges of a dark shape blur at a distance where a human still sees them clearly.
If you are a white-tailed deer, your pupil is a horizontal slit. A reindeer's pupil in bright light is also a bar stretched sideways.
If you are a white-tailed deer, your cones that answer to middle wavelengths crowd into a horizontal streak across the retina. A level band of your view is sharper than the rest.

A reindeer grazing with its eyes turned to a horizontal position has a combined field of about 360 degrees parallel to the ground, and the same is said of deer generally. You very likely see almost all the way round without turning your head.
If you are a white-tailed deer, a reflecting layer behind your retina sends light back through it. Your eyes are specialized for the low light of dawn and dusk, when you are most active.

A reindeer's eye lets some ultraviolet through, and its dark-adapted eyes detect light from 330 to 410 nanometers. Deer in general are very likely sensitive to wavelengths shorter than 400. You very likely see bluish and bright surfaces with a hint of ultraviolet.

Nobody has measured how much sharper your streak is than the edge of your view, or how steeply the blur grows away from it. Nobody has measured how much the reflecting layer lifts a dim scene, or how much of a bluish surface reaches you as ultraviolet. Those amounts, and the way your two cone peaks turn into colors, are guesses.

claims.how: The middle of the 4 to 6 cycles per degree that R3 estimates for white-tailed deer is 5.
R4 states a combined visual field of both eyes of about 360 degrees for Rangifer and other deer.
The matrix is built from the 450 nm low end of the 450 to 460 nm short cone range (R24) and the 537 nm middle cone peak (R26); the mapping to screen colors is the app's.
The peaks 450 nm (low end of the 450 to 460 nm range in R24) and 537 nm (R26) are entered as pigment peaks; the turning of them into color rows is worked out by the engine and is the app's choice.
